FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Metsulfuron methyl + Chlorimuron ethyl wettable powder is a herbicide for agricultural use. Metsulfuron methyl + Chlorimuron ethyl wettable powder is manufactured to contain 10 percent m/m of metsulfuron methyl and 10 percent m/m of chlorimuron ethyl. In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

METSULFURON METHYL+ CHLORIMURON ETHYL WETTABLE POWDER -- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE

This standard _prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for combination formulation of metsuhron methyl + chlorimuron ethyl wettable powder. 2 REFERENCES The followrng standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard . At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are -encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below:
IS No. Title

technical employed in the manufacture of the material shall conform to IS 15615 and IS 15619. 3.2 Physical The material shall complywith the physical.requirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2A. 3.2.1 Description The material shall be a free,free flowing beige coloured homogeneous powder. It shall wet readily on mixing with water, providing a suspension suitable for use as spray. 3.2.2 Sieving Requirements When determined by the method specified in 11.1 of IS .6940, the amount of material passing through 75 micron IS sieve [1S 460 (Part l)], should not be less than 98 percent by mass. 3.2.3 Suspensibility The suspensibility should be not less than 60 percent by mass, when tested by the method specified in 11.2 of IS 6940. 3.2.4 Wettabili~ The time when the whole material gets completely submerged in water should not exceed 120 seconds when tested by the method specified in 11.4of IS 6940. 3.3 Chemical The -material shall also comply with chemical requirements specified in 3.3.1,3.3.2 and 6. 3.3.1 The nominal chlorimuron ethyl and metsulfuron methyl content shall be declared. When determined by the method prescribed in Annex A, the observed metsulfuron methyl content, percent (m/m) and chlorimuron ethyl content, percent (m/m) of any of the samples shall not differ from the declared nominal value by more than the percent tolerance timits indicated below:

3 REQUIREMENTS
3.1 Constituents 3.1.1

The material shall consist of metsulfhron methyl, technical and chlorimuron ethyl technical, together with suitable carrier(s) stabilizer(s) and other formulant(s). 3.1.2 Metsulfuron methyl and chlorimuron ethyl, 1

IS 15618:2005 3.3.2 pH

j)

When tested by the method specified below, the pH of 1 percent m/m solution shall be in the range of 7.0-8.5. Standardize thepH meter with buffer solutions ofpH 4 and 10, or near the pH range of the sample. Weigh accurately 1.0 g of sample material and add to 50 ml of distilled water into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Make up to mark with distilled water. Stopper the flask and shake vigorously for 60 seconds. Transfer the solution to 250 ml beaker. Allow the solution to settle for 60 seconds and immerse the pH electrode into the sample solution. Record the pH of the sample solution after the pH meter stabilizes. 4 PACKING The material shall be packed in -HDPE container (see IS 7328), which shall be heat sealed with HDPE plug and finally closed with HDPE screw cap. The HDPE container can also be sealed with induction sealing system individually. The retail packs shall be further packed in corrugated fibre board boxes [see IS 2771 (Part 1)]. The containers shall also comply with the general requirements specified in IS 8190 (Part 1). 5 MARKING
5.1 The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the

(Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977.

5.2 BIS Certification

Marking

The product may also be marked with the standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producersrnay be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6 SAMPLING When fteshly manufactured-material in bulk quantity and/or the retail pack of the formulated product ishre offered for inspection, representative sample of the material shall be drawn and tested as prescribed in IS 10627 and if tested within 90 days of its date of manufacture, the criteria for conformity shall be the content in percent (m/m), shall not be less than the declared nominal value. The upper limit for conformity shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1 of this standard. When the material is offered for inspection after 90 days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done as prescribed in 4S 10627. However, the -criteria for conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the limit of tolerance, as applicable over the declared nominal value and given in 3.3.1. 7 TESTS
7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred to in 3.2.-1to 3.2.4,3.3.1 and 3.3.2.

ANNEX A (Clause 3.3.1)
DETERMINATION OF METSULFURON METHYL AND C13LORIMURON ETHYL CONTENT A-1 PRINCIPLE A-2 APPARATUS

Metsulfuron methyl and chlorirnuron ethyl content is determined by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using internal standard technique. 2

A high performance liquid chromatography system coupled with ultraviolet detector and a printerplotter-cum-integrator is used for this determination.

A-3.7 Metsulfuron Methyl Analytical Standard, of known purity. A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard

Weigh 4.0 g of phenyl sulfone into a 1000 ml volumetric flask, make up to volume with acetonitrile and ultrasonicate for 10 min. Allow to equilibrate to room temperature prior to use and label the flask. A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution

Weigh accurately 50 mg of metsulfiuon methyl and 50 mg of chlorimuron ethyl analytical standard into a 25 ml volumetric flask. Make up to volume with acetonitrile and ultrasonicate for 15 min. Label the flask as standard stock solution. For preparation of 3

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments. are issued to standards as the need arises .on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'. .
